votes.rationale: SessionTests and HTTPHeaders repeat the same operating-system name/version construction; one helper would centralize normalization and prevent the visible FreeBSD branch from drifting.
Four DataStream tests repeat event, result, and completion capture around the same stream lifecycle; a shared assertion harness would remove the duplicated sequence.
The matching Jazzy search JavaScript is copied into both docs and docset output, so it is generated documentation tooling rather than maintained application code.
Nine empty-body response serializer tests share the same request and assertion flow and vary only serializer, status, method, and expected empty value.
This is another identical Jazzy JavaScript asset emitted into generated docs and docset trees, not a maintainer-owned refactoring target.
Three request lifecycle tests repeat event-monitor installation, expectations, request execution, and teardown; that coherent scaffold belongs in a test helper.
Twenty-four response tests repeat async response capture, waiting, and common response assertions, making a shared response-test harness an actionable reduction.
Request, download, and upload cancellation tests duplicate a long event-monitor and lifecycle-expectation setup that can be shared while leaving transport-specific actions as callbacks.
The SwiftPM manifests target distinct toolchain versions and intentionally carry version-specific tool headers and declarations; merging them would couple compatibility variants.
Two multipart tests construct and assert the same two-file encoded body, so a fixture builder/assertion helper would eliminate the repeated encoding setup.
The same HTML table appears in generated documentation and docset output, which is generated material outside the maintained refactoring surface.
Four DataStream tests repeat session creation, response-stream execution, queue handling, and result assertions; a parameterized stream-test helper can own the common lifecycle.
The two multipart cases duplicate the single-file expected encoding and byte assertion, which can be expressed once as a multipart fixture helper.
The duplicated HTML feature list is emitted in both generated documentation formats, so deduplicating source code would not address it.
Two OfflineRetrier tests repeat monitor setup, four request launches, and identical success assertions; the full scenario is a coherent reusable test helper.
Seven response failure tests share the invalid-URL execution and assertions while varying only serializer or map operation and response type.
ANTLR's parser simulator implements the same algorithm separately in Java and Swift runtimes; a shared abstraction cannot cross those language and runtime boundaries.
Four token-stream tests duplicate grammar input, lexer construction, and token-stream setup, all of which can be centralized in a test fixture factory.
The lexer DFA edge routines are intentionally parallel implementations in ANTLR's Java and Swift runtimes, with runtime-specific types and ownership.
Seven Axios tests repeat server startup, GET execution, response assertion, and finally-stop cleanup; a common server-test helper would remove the lifecycle duplication.
The CommonJS and ESM smoke suites exercise the same transport and progress behavior; a shared behavior harness can accept each module's assertion surface.
Black's gitignore generation tests use one setup and assertion pattern with only ignore patterns and expected paths changing.
This Black formatter fixture intentionally repeats the input below its output marker to record the expected formatting result; deduplication would destroy the fixture contract.
The Chi router cases differ only in where nested middleware is inserted, so one table-driven router test can cover the placement axis.
The exact port_in_range implementation is copied between builder and derive tutorial examples; a shared example utility would prevent behavior drift.
Clap repeats the same override-conflict detection and error construction in three parser paths, which is one coherent helper computation.
Three Clap tests repeat the complete files and target assertion block; a shared parsed-arguments assertion helper would keep the expected contract in one place.
Click's pager and editor paths repeat executable lookup, default-output handling, and path normalization; that preamble is a reusable command-resolution helper.
Cobra tests duplicate child command creation, whitelist configuration, and flag setup; a command-tree fixture factory would remove the repeated arrangement.
Cobra abbreviation tests build the same root, echo, and times command tree and differ only in the input spelling, making the tree a clear helper.
The Java version matcher repeats a long expectation matrix as only the version input advances, which is naturally table-driven.
The patch-version cases repeat the same Java version compatibility matrix with only version constants changing.
The curl Apache module repeats flush-bucket creation, brigade passing, and error handling four times; one brigade-flush helper would centralize that sequence.
Delve DAP tests duplicate breakpoint setup, exception configuration, thread lookup, and protocol handshake; a reusable debug-session scaffold is warranted.
These DAP tests repeat the exception, configuration, and thread-validation sequence, which can be a focused helper independent of each test's final action.
Delve's DWARF type cases repeat name, kind, cache, and referenced-type initialization; a type-construction helper would centralize the invariant fields.
Two Go-version branches duplicate the reverse-step expectation table except for the deferreturn segment, so the version-specific segment can be data.
Five terminal tests share continue, print, log, and assertion flow and vary only the expected integer value.
Seven Delve integration tests repeat error checking, Continue, and state-error validation; a Continue-and-assert helper would remove the sequence.
exc.h and mach_exc.h are MIG-generated Mach interface headers, so their repeated declarations are generated artifacts.
RISC-V single-step and generic Linux hardware single-step loops are architecture-specific signal-control implementations whose differing signal semantics must remain isolated.
Devise timeout tests use the same flow and differ only in destination path and redirect count.
Devise recoverable tests repeat the scenario with only the configured unlock strategy changing.
The model tests duplicate confirmed-user locking setup and the same lock assertions; a locked-confirmed-user fixture would clarify both cases.
The locked-user integration cases differ only in the submitted password, making them a direct input/expectation table.
Twenty-four MySQL generated-column schema tests form a systematic matrix over callback versus SQL expression, stored versus virtual, and add/drop/change operations.
Eight Vercel relational tests repeat the same users and posts seed rows, with only smaller subsets in a few cases; shared fixture tables would remove the literals.
Identical integer boundary constants are copied across the arktype, typebox, valibot, and zod adapters and should come from one limits definition.
Thirty SQLite generated-column tests are a matrix of expression form, storage mode, operation, and expected SQL, ideally represented as one case table.
The migrate command repeats custom-migration writeResult and return handling in five branches; a single result-emission helper would centralize it.
The relational query suite is intentionally repeated for MySQL, Postgres, Vercel, SQLite, PlanetScale, and Turso, whose sync/async and boolean representation quirks differ.
The invitee query case is a backend conformance test copied across database suites, including deliberate sync/async and boolean-versus-number differences.
BetterSQLite tests repeat the same post seed rows eight times within one backend suite, so a shared fixture constant would reduce noise without coupling backends.
Postgres relational tests duplicate the same users and posts fixture in eight cases; one suite-local seed definition is the natural abstraction.
Custom-field relation tests are deliberately mirrored across five database backends to validate backend conformance, and sharing would leak adapter-specific setup.
The many-to-many relation scenarios are backend-specific conformance suites with distinct execution and type semantics despite similar test shape.
The order-by relation tests are primarily parallel backend variants, and the one overlapping adjacent member does not create a coherent cross-backend helper.
The MySQL integration file repeats full users/posts schema creation and index setup four times; a suite-local schema fixture would remove substantial arrangement code.
The Execa type-test files only share imports and a constant declaration; extracting that boilerplate would add indirection without a meaningful behavior abstraction.
Faraday JSON parsing cases share the same body and assertions and differ only in whether raw response bodies are preserved.
Fastlane.swift is a generated-style action wrapper surface, and the duplicated sigh alias wrapper is not hand-maintained business logic to deduplicate.
Fastlane's create-PR action repeats the same GitHub error-to-payload handling block four times; one error-response helper would keep those responses consistent.
Two specs repeat the exact Bad Gateway HTML document and setup; a named response fixture would make the scenario clearer and eliminate the large literal.
Git's compat/obstack.c is vendored GNU libc code, confirmed by its upstream copyright header, and should not be locally refactored.
The duplicated local inline setter is only four lines in separate C translation units; a shared abstraction would cost more coupling than it saves.
Git's inflate and deflate wrappers share loop termination, status mapping, and error handling, differing mainly in operation and label.
The reftable rename and copy functions perform the same execution with only the delete_old argument changing.
fast-import's file-change and note-change parsers repeat dataref, inline-data, and object parsing; a shared data-reference parser is coherent.
update-ref repeats delimiter validation and input advancement in parse_next_refname and parse_next_arg, which should be one token-consumption helper.
The PtIsochrone tests differ only in whether the point is supplied as coordinates or a station, while the route expectations are the same.
The waypoint and stop circle CSS classes share all declarations except border color; a common base selector with color overrides would remove the copy.
Three GraphHopper path tests repeat roundabout angle extraction and assertion; a focused angle assertion helper would expose the varying path only.
Gson malformed-Unicode tests repeat reader setup and exception assertion while varying only malformed input and expected message.
Gson serialization paths repeat the exact strictness-application block, which is one reusable configuration operation.
Two MapTypeAdapter branches repeat key/value reading, duplicate-key detection, and map insertion; a shared entry-reading helper would prevent divergent handling.
JsonReader and JsonWriter setLenient methods are matching compatibility wrappers on unrelated final classes, with no clean shared owner for one tiny method.
Three closed-JsonWriter tests differ only in the attempted operation—name, value, or flush—and can be a single operation table.
The six-line serialization assertion is repeated for two distinct naming strategies, but extracting it would obscure simple local expectations for negligible savings.
nextUnquotedValue and skipUnquotedValue are purpose-specific hot loops with different output and position semantics; sharing would compromise their optimized control flow.
ForwardingBlockingDeque is mirrored across Android/JRE and deprecated/current package surfaces for compatibility, so the copies are intentional platform/API variants.
HashingTest is an exact Android/JRE source-tree mirror used to validate both platform builds, not one suite accidentally copied.
ImmutableMap and BiMap tests combine API-specific variants with Android/JRE mirrors; merging them would conflate distinct invariants and platforms.
SourceSinkTester is intentionally mirrored between Android and JRE test trees, including platform compatibility annotations.
The benchmark is an Android/JRE mirror whose duplication is the build and platform layout rather than a missing code abstraction.
CacheStatsTest is copied across Android and JRE suites to exercise each platform artifact independently.
WriteReplaceOverridesTest is an intentional Android/JRE mirror required by the parallel source-set design.
XmlEscapersTest is mirrored across platform source sets so each Guava build validates the same contract independently.
The FinalizableReferenceQueue unloading test is an Android/JRE source-set mirror rather than duplicated logic within one maintained component.
RowMap test classes cover submap, headmap, tailmap, transformed, and unmodifiable variants plus platform mirrors; their per-variant setup is intentional.
AbstractIterator tests span base versus collect APIs and Android/JRE mirrors, so a shared helper would couple intentionally separate compatibility surfaces.
Hugo's go_templates exec tests state that they are copied from the Go Authors text/template suite, making this vendored upstream test code.
Two Hugo resource-chain cases repeat a roughly 65-line virtual site and asset fixture; one shared fixture definition would materially simplify both.
BMP OS/2v2 and info-header readers repeat applying ParsedInfoHeader fields and checking overflow; that conversion is one coherent helper.
Jekyll setup cases differ only in selected document index and destination while sharing the build and assertion flow.
Jekyll default-scope tests vary only the path and nested expected value, making them straightforward table cases.
Four Jest fake-timer tests repeat extended fake-global construction and timer initialization; a fixture factory would centralize the environment.
Four additional fake-timer cases repeat the basic fake-global, timer construction, and activation sequence.
Three Jest stack-message tests differ only in noCodeFrame and noStackTrace flags while asserting the same formatting behavior.
Three inline-snapshot tests repeat the file fixture and frame list, varying only the Prettier mode.
jq's array and object getters share only a short optional-slot copy, while their ownership and key/index handling remain distinct.
Four JUnit suite tests repeat the exact UniqueId construction chain; a named UniqueId fixture would make the shared hierarchy explicit.
The four-line static @Parameters method is framework-mandated boilerplate in five fixture classes, and extracting it would not remove the required declarations.
Two standalone launcher tests repeat a 14-line Java command argument and execution chain that belongs in a launcher test utility.
libsodium duplicates constant-time field conditional operations inside specialized cryptographic routines; extraction could disturb algorithm and timing invariants.
These libsodium field-reduction tails live in specialized constant-time routines whose local arithmetic layout is part of their design.
fe25519_sq and fe25519_sq2 are deliberately specialized constant-time primitives, with the latter doubling output; a shared helper risks performance and auditability.
Scalar multiplication and multiply-add share declarations but implement different cryptographic operations whose arithmetic routines are intentionally self-contained.
This is another field-reduction tail embedded in specialized libsodium arithmetic, where local duplication preserves constant-time audited code.
SHA3, SHAKE, and TurboSHAKE absorb loops differ only in rate and permutation-round counts; one Keccak absorb helper can take those parameters.
Mockito's invalid annotation-combination tests can share the thrown-exception and message assertion harness while retaining distinct annotated fixture classes.
Nine NATS file-store tests repeat stop, delete-state, reopen, and recovered-state assertions; a recovery helper would centralize the lifecycle.
Six file-store tests repeat creation and population loops with only message count and error-checking mode changing.
A very large set of JetStream tests repeats basic server and client startup plus cleanup; composable t.Cleanup-based fixtures would remove substantial suite-wide boilerplate.
Three NATS stretch-cluster tests repeat cluster, client, stream, and leader setup, which is a coherent cluster scenario fixture.
Three OCSP test tables repeat config-file creation, server startup, connection, and expected-error handling; a shared runner can own that lifecycle.
Two OCSP table cases duplicate a full server configuration and client option array, which should be named shared test data.
HAProxy decoder tests duplicate the same 28-byte v2 header and vary only the protocol byte and expected enum.
Five JNI QUIC path-event wrappers share the same conversion body and differ only in the native event extraction function.
Ten SSL tests repeat the SslContextBuilder server prefix; a suite helper can construct the common server context before per-test customization.
Sixteen OpenSSL session-stat getters repeat the same read-lock and try/finally wrapper around one native call; a locked-stat helper would centralize safety.
The family consists only of seven common Java imports across unrelated examples and tests, with no behavior to abstract.
Eight UTF-8 surrogate tests repeat buffer allocation, write, assert, and release flow while only the character sequence changes.
Encoder/decoder by River/Serial subclasses are protocol-direction variants with distinct base classes and configuration versions, intentionally kept parallel.
Three CompositeByteBuf input overloads repeat the cross-component setBytes loop; only the input read operation needs to be supplied to a helper.
Seven channel-pipeline tail tests repeat custom channel, bootstrap, connect, latch, and cleanup setup; a reusable pipeline fixture would reduce the common lifecycle.
The JNI loop is deliberately unrolled for four position/limit field-versus-method access combinations, preserving variant-specific performance measurements.
Eight primitive-array append methods are required Java primitive overload boilerplate; a shared abstraction cannot remove the public overload surface.
HTTP upstream primary and backup loops repeat dynamic-host peer allocation and initialization; one peer-construction helper would keep both paths aligned.
The HTTP write filter repeats full zero-size buffer validation and logging in two chain scans, which is a coherent validation helper.
Stream upstream primary and backup loops repeat host-peer allocation and initialization just as the HTTP module does; a module-local peer helper is actionable.
gRPC and HTTP proxy v2 modules separately parse GOAWAY, WINDOW_UPDATE, and RST_STREAM frames using different context types and state enums; sharing would couple backend modules.
Win32 and Unix select event modules expose parallel platform implementations with platform-specific state and limits, so the matching structure is intentional.
The stream write filter repeats zero-size buffer validation and logging in two chain passes; one validator would remove the duplicated safety logic.
Nushell's four comparison operators repeat Nothing propagation and compatible-type error construction, differing only in the comparison enum.
Five completion tests repeat Windows slash normalization and the same suggestion assertions; a path-suggestion assertion helper would centralize cross-platform handling.
Six Polars conversion branches repeat iterator slicing, None handling, and collection, with only the value conversion closure varying.
The repeated run methods are mandatory trait implementations for separate parser test command fixtures and contain only todo boilerplate.
Two Poetry executor tests duplicate package construction, source-type branching, execution, and output checks, varying only config_settings versus build_constraints.
Poetry's config listing tests repeat the full expected configuration text and differ chiefly by the optional repository line.
The empty- and non-empty-directory init tests duplicate interactive inputs and all project-structure assertions; a common init-and-assert helper would leave only preconditions distinct.
The optional-chaining JSX and TSX snippets are formatter fixtures intentionally enumerating syntax and language variants, so merging them would erase cases.
The repeated Flow AST fields are pure union-member type declarations with no behavior to extract.
These Flow refinement snippets intentionally form a matrix over null, typeof, undefined, and void checks and property depths for formatter coverage.
The matching FunctionDeclaration and FunctionExpression blocks are repeated structural members in a Flow AST union type, not executable behavior.
Eight Prometheus histogram cases repeat identical spans and bucket literals; a named histogram fixture would reduce large test-data copies.
Five FloatHistogram test entries duplicate the complete threshold, counts, spans, and buckets structure, which should be one reusable fixture value.
Three Consul tests repeat the exact HTTP path-switch mock and filter capture; a shared mock handler would prevent endpoint behavior from drifting.
Fifteen PromQL documentation entries repeat the same deg, pi, and rad JSX list; a reusable documentation fragment component would own it.
Ten OpenAPI schema builders repeat warning/info properties and identical object-schema construction, varying only description and required fields.
Three Rack multipart tests repeat request environment construction and form-pair extraction; a multipart form_pairs helper would leave only input and expectation.
stb_image_resize2.h is vendored third-party single-header code, so its coefficient-specialized routines are not Raylib-maintained deduplication targets.
The repeated FLAC conversion preamble is inside vendored miniaudio.h, a third-party single-header dependency.
The repeated mid/side sample conversion block belongs to vendored miniaudio.h and should be changed upstream, not refactored locally.
The repeated WAV open/read wrappers are in the vendored miniaudio single-header library, outside Raylib's maintained code.
These unrolled FLAC mid/side conversion blocks are third-party miniaudio code and therefore not a local refactoring opportunity.
The complete rlights implementation is duplicated between two Raylib example directories; one shared example header would eliminate a 170-line copy.
Raylib's MatrixInvert and rlMatrixInvert bodies are identical 4x4 inversion algorithms; a shared internal inversion implementation would prevent numerical fixes from diverging.
Requests' two __exit__ methods are identical two-line context-manager delegations to close, and sharing them would add more structure than code.
Retrofit's jaxb and jaxb3 converter artifacts intentionally target javax and Jakarta JAXB packages; sharing would couple separate compatibility modules.
Two Rich progress tests repeat Console, Progress, and temporary-file setup; a test fixture helper would remove the arrangement block.
Rich duplicates the same span-clamping comprehension in _trim_spans and right_crop; routing both through one trimming helper would centralize boundary semantics.
Rich's open and wrap_file paths repeat progress-column construction and Progress initialization; a progress-builder helper can serve both reader entry points.
Style.copy, clear_meta_and_links, and update_link repeat allocation and core-field copying; a private clone initializer can accept link/meta/hash overrides.
Bar and ProgressBar each implement a simple width-to-Measurement protocol method; introducing a base solely for this small conditional would over-couple the classes.
The CRLF regression test runs the same search and output assertion before and after enabling replacement; a local run-and-assert helper would make the two modes explicit.
RSpec aggregate-failure tests repeat example execution and nested exception matching; a helper can accept the failure blocks and expected exception matchers.
Three RuboCop injector specs repeat a large generated source expectation and differ only in the inserted require and message.
Six assignment specs repeat source fixture and nil assertion while varying only the Ruby assignment form.
Seven target-finder specs duplicate config doubles, exclusion setup, and basename assertions; a suite helper can own the common exclusion scenario.
Two unused-method-argument contexts repeat the message builder, offense markup, and correction expectation; a shared RSpec example would remove the exact block.
Two RuboCop server CLI contexts contain the same file creation, invocation, and stdout/stderr assertions; a shared example is directly applicable.
Two Scrapy subprocess fixtures duplicate the reactor-check extension, no-request spider, and AsyncCrawlerProcess run; a helper module can be invoked after each file's reactor precondition.
Four Scrapy proxy redirect tests are a matrix over HTTP/HTTPS and absolute/relative redirects with the same three-request authorization assertions.
Sinatra before- and after-filter tests repeat static-file and route-pattern scenarios, differing only in the filter hook.
SQLite speedtest repeats the same randomized number-name binding loop for three prepared statements; a benchmark runner helper can own that loop.
SQLite's VFS instrumentation functions are interface adapters with operation-specific signatures, calls, and log payloads; a shared wrapper would leak per-method quirks.
seriesColumn is copied into a WASM amalgamation and fuzzing shell alongside its source extension, so the family is dominated by generated or embedded copies.
JoinedBySequence and JoinedByCollection are intentional API and performance variants over distinct Swift protocols and inner collection types.
Grouped and keyed tests repeat the same throwing-key closure and identity assertion; a generic test helper can accept the operation under test.
Two completion cases repeat an async call, expected-failure guard, and XCTFail fallback; an assertCustomCompletionFails helper would express the intent once.
Three SplitArguments removal tests have identical count and index assertions and vary only the initial argument array.
Two Swift Argument Parser tools carry near-identical Process execution utilities; a shared tool-support module can parameterize stderr capture and compatibility behavior.

GenerateDoccReference and GenerateManual duplicate output-directory validation, subprocess decoding, version checking, and output routing; a shared generation pipeline can accept tool-specific errors and rendering.
Eight OrderedSet benchmark registrations form a matrix over set operation and Self versus Array operand; a generic registration helper can take title and operation closures.
Eight BigString benchmarks repeat the distance-validation loop for Character, UnicodeScalar, UTF8, and UTF16 views across two input groups.
Eight mutating Set benchmarks vary only operation and Self versus Array operand while sharing registration, construction, timing, and black-hole handling.
InputSpan and OutputSpan insert overloads are repeated across RigidArray, RigidDeque, and UniqueDeque container APIs, with ownership-direction semantics tied to each type.
Eight mutating OrderedSet benchmarks are the same overlap registration scaffold parameterized by operation and operand collection type.
Six OrderedSet relation tests repeat range setup and generic Sequence bridging while only the relation predicate changes.
The two public replace overloads duplicate mostly required API documentation; their executable bodies are short delegations distinguished by generic constraints.
Eight nonmutating Set benchmark blocks vary only set operation and Self versus Array operand, making one generic benchmark registration table appropriate.
The moving replace overloads are required across three container implementations and InputSpan/OutputSpan ownership directions; the parallel API surface is intentional.
Four MinimalEncoder container types repeat a five-line memberwise initializer that Swift requires on each distinct nested type.
Four minimal collection fixtures deliberately model different RandomAccess, Mutable, and RangeReplaceable protocol combinations; a shared base would undermine the independent conformance fixtures.
TreeDictionary's overloads duplicate extensive required API documentation, while the actual implementation is only a four-line copy-and-merge delegation.
The matching reducer cases are progressive tutorial snapshots whose stage-by-stage self-contained source is the documentation design.
Four presentation reducer tests duplicate a local Parent reducer and TestStore scaffold around different Child behaviors; a reusable presentation-test fixture can parameterize the child.
These complete RecordMeeting files are previous/current progressive tutorial snapshots; sharing them would erase the exact code state readers are meant to compare.
The four identical SyncUpsList files are consecutive self-contained tutorial stages and previous snapshots, intentionally preserving each stage's full source.
Nine EffectOperation tests repeat operation pattern matching, async send, and XCTFail handling; a generic assertion helper can take the expected payload.
Twenty SyncUpDetail files are incremental tutorial snapshots with deliberately repeated surrounding code and stage-specific additions.
The TrailingIconLabelStyle implementation is repeated mainly across self-contained tutorial snapshots plus the finished example; the copies track tutorial stages by design.

AttributeEnrichingHandler and AttributeStrippingHandler duplicate all LogHandler forwarding and differ only in event metadata transformation; a shared forwarding handler or trait can own the common surface.
Two global logging tests repeat the exact seven expected log records; a shared expectation table and assertion loop would keep the contract in one place.
Three SwiftLint enable-all tests repeat the violating-phrase loop and count assertion, varying only placement of enable, previous, or next directives.
Two custom-rule configuration tests differ only in match_kinds versus excluded_match_kinds and the expected SyntaxKind set.
assertNoViolation and assert1Violation are intentional convenience wrappers already delegating to assertViolations; their duplication is mostly unavoidable default-argument forwarding.
The four visitor constructors only assign one subclass-specific field and delegate to super, which is standard initializer boilerplate across unrelated visitor types.
TrailingWhitespaceRule repeats position advancement and block-comment coverage marking in two adjacent piece loops; a piece-consumption helper would centralize it.
Four SWR middleware tests duplicate logger middleware, Page component, rendering, and common assertions; a middleware behavior harness can accept key, fetcher, and configuration placement.
The four SWR E2E pages are separate suspense scenarios whose shared imports and tiny delayed fetchers are page-fixture boilerplate, while their behavior remains distinct.
Three Thor sort specs repeat command-class creation, help capture, and ordering assertion; only the sort override and expected order change.
tmux's clear-to-end, clear-to-start, and clear-screen paths repeat obscured-pane cursor and window-offset initialization; a helper can return the saved cursor and offsets.
Four tmux window and pane commands repeat spawn-context cleanup and error return after creation failure; one cleanup-and-report helper would prevent resource-handling drift.
Vapor ClientRequest and ClientResponse duplicate content decode, afterDecode, and content-container synchronization; a shared content-container adapter can serve both.
Two Vapor middleware metric assertions repeat the exact seven OpenTelemetry attributes; a named expected-attributes fixture would remove the literal copy.
Four Vapor basic-auth tests duplicate authenticator types, route setup, credentials, and response checks while varying password and unauthorized middleware behavior.
Two Zap encoder cases repeat the same EncoderConfig field mapping; constructing a common abbreviated config and overriding time behavior would avoid the copy.
Two Zustand devtools tests repeat four connection option objects and four initial states; a shared grouped-store fixture would centralize this test data.
